name: OpenMathReasoning
intro: OpenMathReasoning 是 NVIDIA 面向数学推理模型后训练发布的数据集，而非固定独立评测集。论文 v1 从 AoPS 论坛的 620K 条讨论，经 Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 抽取、分类、格式过滤、证明题转换、答案抽取和基准去污染，报告流水线阶段 540K 个问题；固定官方 HF v1.0 发布卡随后更正为 306K 个具有公开解答的问题，并另含 193,170 条仅问题记录。发布共 5,678,317 行：3,201,061 条 CoT、1,718,466 条 TIR、565,620 条 GenSelect 及 193,170 条额外问题。
build_method: AoPS讨论采集；Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct问题抽取、分类、过滤、证明题转换、答案抽取与基准去污染；DeepSeek-R1/QwQ-32B长思维链生成和答案等价过滤；迭代工具集成推理；GenSelect构建
metric: 数据集无内在基准分；论文在 AIME24、AIME25、HMMT-24-25 与 HLE-Math 上报告 pass@1、maj@64 和 GenSelect 变体准确率
openness: public; CC-BY-4.0 dataset and Apache-2.0 reproduction code
task_type: 数学推理训练数据, 思维链, 工具集成推理, 解答选择
eval_feature: 训练数据构建；明确区分论文540K流水线问题与HF v1.0中306K个有解问题；在外部数学基准上对OpenMath-Nemotron进行64次生成评测，而非评测OpenMathReasoning测试集
scale: HF v1.0共5,678,317行：3,201,061 CoT、1,718,466 TIR、565,620 GenSelect、193,170额外仅问题记录；306K个问题具有公开解答
openness_en: Public; CC-BY-4.0 Dataset and Apache-2.0 Reproduction Code
task_type_en: Mathematical-reasoning Training Data, Chain of Thought, Tool-integrated Reasoning, Solution Selection
build_method_en: AoPS Discussion Collection; Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct Extraction, Classification, Filtering, Proof Conversion, Answer Extraction, and Benchmark Decontamination; DeepSeek-R1/QwQ-32B Long-CoT Generation and Answer-equivalence Filtering; Iterative TIR; GenSelect Construction
eval_feature_en: Training-data Construction; Paper-stage 540K Problems Explicitly Reconciled with 306K Solution-bearing Problems in HF v1.0; 64-generation Evaluation of OpenMath-Nemotron on External Math Benchmarks Rather than an OpenMathReasoning Test Set
intro_en: OpenMathReasoning is NVIDIA post-training data for mathematical-reasoning models, not a fixed standalone evaluation benchmark. Paper v1 starts from 620K AoPS forum discussions and applies Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct extraction, classification, format filtering, proof conversion, answer extraction, and benchmark decontamination, reporting 540K problems at the pipeline stage. The fixed official HF v1.0 card later corrects the released solution-bearing scope to 306K problems and adds 193,170 problem-only records. Its 5,678,317 rows comprise 3,201,061 CoT, 1,718,466 TIR, 565,620 GenSelect, and 193,170 additional-problem rows.
scale_en: HF v1.0 has 5,678,317 rows: 3,201,061 CoT, 1,718,466 TIR, 565,620 GenSelect, and 193,170 additional problem-only rows; released solutions cover 306K problems
metric_en: No intrinsic dataset benchmark score; the paper reports pass@1, maj@64, and GenSelect-variant accuracy on AIME24, AIME25, HMMT-24-25, and HLE-Math

drawio_review_note: source_stage=paper-alignment; reviewed_at=2026-07-22; benchmark=OpenMathReasoning; formal_assets_intentionally_not_modified=true. Paper evidence: arXiv:2504.16891 has one submission only, v1 dated 2025-04-23. The fixed PDF URL is https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.16891v1 and the downloaded 39-page PDF SHA256 is c4eeeb75e86af3d7b6e35ad3e9ade1d339cd481da7f6121c9a600742c0c9ed4c. Sections 2-4 are treated as the construction and downstream-evaluation contract. The paper collects 620K AoPS discussions from every forum except Middle School Math, uses Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct to extract zero, one, or several problems per post, obtains 580K extracted problems, classifies proof/non-proof, multiple-choice/binary, and valid/invalid status, removes bad formats to 550K, converts proofs to answer questions, extracts final answers when possible, and uses LLM comparison against popular math benchmarks for decontamination, yielding the paper-stage 540K figure. Long-CoT evidence: the paper generates up to 32 candidate solutions per problem with DeepSeek-R1 and QwQ-32B at temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.95. Candidates are checked against extracted expected answers; where no answer was extracted, the majority answer is used, and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct judges answer equivalence. The paper reports roughly 2.7M retained DeepSeek-R1 solutions plus 0.5M QwQ-32B solutions. The fixed HF metadata gives the precise cot split count as 3,201,061 rows. TIR evidence: the paper seeds tool-integrated reasoning by prompting LIMO-Qwen-32B to use Python, synthesizes about 1.2M candidates, filters these to 15K stage-0 samples, and iterates model training, generation, execution, and quality filtering. The final paper figure is 1.7M TIR solutions; the fixed HF metadata gives 1,718,466 rows. GenSelect evidence: candidate solutions are sampled, concise faithful summaries are prepared, QwQ-32B selects promising candidates, and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct rewrites summaries used as outputs. The paper reports 566K examples; the fixed HF metadata gives 565,620 rows. Release-count drift: the paper v1 repeatedly reports 540K unique problems, but the official dataset card explicitly says this was the question count at the beginning of the pipeline. At HF revision d3d08664755704f422af97d43a7ff0ded4bd95df, the solution-bearing CoT/TIR release covers 306K unique problems and a separate additional_problems split contains 193,170 problem-only rows. The card attributes the difference to subsequent format restrictions, benchmark decontamination, inability to generate valid solutions for some problems, and a pipeline bug that lost 137K proof-based questions. It also states that OpenMath-Nemotron models were trained on the reduced solution-bearing subset, so published results remain reproducible. The graph therefore keeps paper_scope and release_scope as distinct nodes, connects them sequentially, and adds a dashed count-correction boundary instead of silently replacing one count with the other. HF snapshot evidence: official dataset revision d3d08664755704f422af97d43a7ff0ded4bd95df was resolved with git ls-remote. The pinned README at that revision has SHA256 976666d0a4848732990c96e3b1111ec4938f215b212b3ee8231ad10052d905e6. Its metadata records 3,201,061 cot, 1,718,466 tir, 565,620 genselect, and 193,170 additional_problems rows, totaling 5,678,317. It declares Data Version 1.0 dated 2025-04-23 and license cc-by-4.0. These metadata counts are treated as release facts; the full 49.6 GB download was not repeated in this source-stage review. Code snapshot evidence: the official card links NVIDIA NeMo Skills as the reproduction pipeline. HEAD resolved to 74b8649734a6ecc2d3beca89311e1a5e02da48fa. The pinned README SHA256 is 1902964e40bcca625986e5fd8dda28b2c229878ab8efd10995b7b33f5a85c9cc and the pinned LICENSE SHA256 is c71d239df91726fc519c6eb72d318ec65820627232b2f796219e87dcf35d0ab4, declaring Apache License 2.0. This is separate from the HF dataset CC BY 4.0 license. The graph uses a dashed license boundary so code and data terms are not collapsed into a single openness label. Evaluation evidence: OpenMathReasoning itself is training data. The paper trains OpenMath-Nemotron 1.5B, 7B, 14B, and 32B models and evaluates them on external AIME24, AIME25, HMMT-24-25, and a 975-item text-only HLE-Math subset. It generates 64 answers per problem with temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95 and reports pass@1 as average accuracy over 64 generations and maj@64 as majority-vote accuracy, with CoT, TIR, and GenSelect variants reported separately. AIMO-2 is a downstream competition use case, not an OpenMathReasoning held-out test set. The dashed role boundary prevents presentation as a standalone fixed benchmark or leaderboard. Diagram contract: English and Chinese specs use the same 24 node IDs, 23 edges, node types, sizes, coordinates, and edge styles. Construction nodes are evidence, source, extract, classify, filter, transform, decontam, paper_scope, release_scope, cot_generate, cot_filter, cot_release, tir_seed, tir_iterate, genselect, and release. Evaluation nodes are train_models, eval_suite, sample64, aggregate, and report. Boundary nodes are count_boundary, license_boundary, and role_boundary. All four secondary edges explicitly set style.dashed=true. English labels contain no Han characters; every Chinese node contains Chinese semantics. The detail Mermaid fallbacks are generated exactly from the two source specs. Formal Draw.io, arch JSON, SVG, PNG, catalog, manifest, queue reports, and sync scripts are intentionally outside this source-stage patch. Formal publication evidence [site-a12b-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 1653×1185 (English) and 1654×1185 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 1651×1183 and 1652×1183. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
